drivingQuestion: When the slaughter itself was performed improperly, is the animal a neveila that imparts ritual impurity or only a tereifa?
outcomeNote: Rabbi Akiva concedes to Rabbi Yeshevav once the principle is stated in Rabbi Yehoshua's name, so the mishna ends with the neveila ruling standing.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ שָׁחַט אֶת הַוֶּושֶׁט, וּפָסַק אֶת הַגַּרְגֶּרֶת, אוֹ פָסַק אֶת הַגַּרְגֶּרֶת וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁחַט אֶת הַוֶּושֶׁט, אוֹ שָׁחַט אֶחָד מֵהֶן וְהִמְתִּין לָהּ עַד שֶׁמֵּתָה, אוֹ שֶׁהֶחְלִיד אֶת הַסַּכִּין תַּחַת הַשֵּׁנִי וּפְסָקוֹ – רַבִּי יְשֵׁבָב אוֹמֵר: נְבֵלָה, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: טְרֵפָה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» If «one cut the gullet» in the standard manner of slaughter with a back-and-forth movement, «and he severed the windpipe» not in the standard manner, «or» if «one severed the windpipe and thereafter cut the gullet, or» if «one cut one of» the simanim «and waited until» the animal «died, or» if one cut one siman and «concealed the knife beneath the second» siman «and severed it» from below, «Rabbi Yeshevav says:» The animal is «an unslaughtered carcass» and imparts ritual impurity through contact with it and carrying it. «Rabbi Akiva says:» The animal is «a tereifa,» and although eating it is prohibited, it does not transmit ritual impurity.

segments.he: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי יְשֵׁבָב מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: כֹּל שֶׁנִּפְסְלָה בִּשְׁחִיטָתָהּ – נְבֵלָה, כֹּל שֶׁשְּׁחִיטָתָהּ כָּרָאוּי וְדָבָר אַחֵר גָּרַם לָהּ לִיפָּסֵל – טְרֵפָה, וְהוֹדָה לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yeshevav stated a principle in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua: Any» animal «that was rendered unfit during its slaughter» because the slaughter was not performed properly «is an unslaughtered carcass; any» animal «whose slaughter was» performed «properly and another matter caused it to become unfit is a tereifa. And Rabbi Akiva conceded to his» opinion.

moves.cueHe: שחט את הוושט, ופסק את הגרגרת
moves.summary: lists four defective slaughters — severing the windpipe out of order, waiting until the animal died, concealing the knife
moves.about: whether an animal whose slaughter was itself botched is an unslaughtered carcass that imparts ritual impurity, or only a tereifa that is forbidden to eat

moves.summary: Rabbi Yeshevav rules the animal a carcass that imparts impurity
Rabbi Akiva rules it a tereifa, forbidden but not defiling

moves.cueHe: כלל אמר רבי ישבב משום רבי יהושע
moves.summary: generalizes his position as a principle received from Rabbi Yehoshua: unfitness in the slaughter makes a carcass, unfitness from another cause a tereifa
moves.about: Rabbi Yeshevav states the general principle distinguishing neveila from tereifa in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua
Rabbi Akiva accepts Rabbi Yeshevav's principle that a slaughter invalidated in the act makes the animal a carcass
